task: Build a lightweight dev-memory layer so useful lessons from ordinary non-Koala Claude/Codex/Gemini programming sessions can be captured and surfaced before later development starts.
outcome: A user can capture a concrete failure-mode lesson, search/list it, see a bounded preflight context pack before new work, finish a session with story-scoped candidate lessons, and run a dev-start wrapper that shows relevant lessons without treating them as gate evidence.
facts: User concern from 2026-05-29: valuable design-process/failure-mode/success-pattern experience is currently lost when a coding session does not use a Koala story.

Anchor case: during previous Koala delegation, long Claude CLI reviewer prompts could stall or return late; the durable lesson is to use short single-responsibility prompts and verify with git/status/test evidence instead of natural-language confidence.
Koala already has authoritative story/checklist/evidence/gate/process-events; dev-memory must complement these and must not become DONE evidence.
Existing home-scoped file-backed precedent exists in ~/.koala/health.jsonl, and story capsule already separates current projection from authoritative evidence.
CLI command schemas are declared in packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts and handlers are registered through packages/main/src/registry.ts.

PLAN unknowns were resolved during code inspection: commands will be Koala-native, storage will be project/global JSONL, wrappers will default to prompt-only/dry-run output, and dev-memory will not modify process-fact-registry because it is not gate evidence.
constraints: Experience memory is reusable context only, not authority evidence, not review pass, not validation evidence, and not a lifecycle gate input.
Use simple inspectable JSONL/Markdown files; no vector database, daemon, UI, or external service in this story.
Preflight output is bounded to at most 5 entries and 60 terminal lines to avoid token bloat.
Duplicate or near-duplicate capture should warn and link to the existing entry rather than silently creating another authoritative-looking fact.
Active story detection order is explicit --storyId, KOALA_STORY_ID, then current cwd/session context; unclear story context degrades to project/global memory only.
Tests must use temp project/home paths and must not pollute real user memory.
